title: 3rd case: 'by means of' and 'with'

video.title: तृतीया विभक्ति
video.focus: Listen for the main idea: तृतीया = 'by means of / with' (करण), and सह ('together with') takes तृतीया. Note the -एन ending.

recap: Your Day 20 answers (quiz and 10 sentences) didn't come in, so here's a warm-up first. W1: Say 'I am a student.' W2: Which verb goes with वयम् (we all): पठामः, पठावः or पठथ? W3: Translate: 'Do you read Sanskrit?' Your 10 sentences are still welcome; send them any time.
idea: A **case (विभक्ति, vibhakti)** is an ending on a noun that shows its job in the sentence. Hindi puts a small word after the noun (ने, को, से, का); Sanskrit changes the noun's ending instead. Sanskrit has 7 cases; today is the 3rd, **तृतीया (tṛtīyā)**.
The 3rd case marks the thing you use to do something. Hindi: हाथ **से** लिखता है. Sanskrit: **हस्तेन** लिखति.
## The endings for -a nouns (masculine and neuter)
**Sound note:** when र, ऋ or ष comes earlier in the word, the न usually becomes ण: रामेण, मित्रेण, पुत्रेण (but हस्तेन, बालकेन). The exact rule comes later.
सह (saha) = के साथ. The person you are with goes in the 3rd case: **मित्रेण सह** गच्छति = दोस्त के साथ जाता है.
**Careful:** Hindi से means both 'with' and 'from'. Sanskrit splits them: 'with / by' is the 3rd case; 'from' is the 5th case (Day 23).
**Video note:** the video uses exam terms (करण कारक, उपपद विभक्ति). You don't need to memorise them. If it says तृतीया marks the doer, that is only in passive sentences (Day 51).

quiz.q: What is the 3rd case singular of बालकः?
quiz.why: -a nouns take -एन in the 3rd case singular. बालकम् is the 2nd case; बालकस्य is the 6th.

quiz.q: Which sentence means 'Rama goes with (his) friends'?
quiz.why: सह needs the 3rd case; the plural 3rd case of मित्र is मित्रैः.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank with हस्त: सः ___ लिखति। (He writes with his hand.)
quiz.why: The tool you write with goes in the 3rd case: हस्तेन.

quiz.q: Why is it मित्रेण but हस्तेन?
options: Because र comes earlier in मित्र, so न becomes ण
quiz.why: र, ऋ or ष earlier in the word usually turns a later न into ण (रामेण, मित्रेण).

quiz.q: Translate into Sanskrit: I eat with a spoon.
quiz.why: अहम् (I) + चमसेन (with a spoon, 3rd case) + खादामि (I eat).
